This letter discloses a data incident affecting a subset of customer accounts between March 3 and March 11. We believe, though have not fully confirmed, that the exposure was limited to email addresses and hashed passwords; we have found no evidence that payment card data was accessed, but we are not yet in a position to rule it out entirely.

We engaged an outside forensics firm on March 12, the day after our internal monitoring flagged unusual database export activity. Their preliminary findings, which remain subject to revision as the investigation continues, indicate the access originated from a compromised contractor credential that should have been deactivated in January and was not.

We are resetting passwords for all affected accounts and requiring re-authentication on next login. If you reused your password on another service, we recommend changing it there as well, since we cannot verify from our side whether it was also compromised elsewhere.

We recognize this falls short of what you should be able to expect from us, and we are retaining the same firm to review our credential offboarding process, not only this specific failure.
